label: <DEL> step of length-3 sequences, gated by token identity (first token k/v/h/l/2/n, third token f/q/w/digit)
explanation: Very sparse (about 0.013% of steps). About 97% of activation mass is at the delimiter step (t = L) and over 99% is in L=3 sequences; it essentially never fires during the original phase or later in the copy phase, or for L >= 4. (phase==1)&(L==3) alone gets recall 0.89 and mass recall 0.97 but precision only 0.06, so within L=3 delimiters firing depends on which tokens were seen. It is strongest when the first token is k or v (also h, l, 2, n) and the third (last) token is f, q or w (also 0, 1, z, c); the top examples are k 2 f, v 2 f, v k c, k h f, v 2 w. The second token (k, 2, d, l, o, h) also matters to a lesser degree. This token conjunction is only approximate (dev F1 0.53, mass recall 0.70). A loose 2-of-3 token-set version reaches mass recall 0.95 with precision 0.34. Small residual firing at t=2 and t=4 of L=3 sequences.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: k, v, l, 2, h, n; least: t, g, -, b) and the previous input (most: f, q, 0, w, 1, c; least: g, j, s, u); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=3, t=2.
